content.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent Ratios
content.overview: This lesson covers the fundamental trigonometric ratios—sine, cosine, and tangent—within right triangles. These ratios relate the measures of acute angles to the lengths of the triangle's sides.
learning_objectives: Identify the opposite side, adjacent side, and hypotenuse relative to a specific acute angle.
Define and calculate the sine, cosine, and tangent ratios for a given angle.
Simplify trigonometric fractions and verify tangent using the sine-to-cosine relationship.

sections.title: Labeling the Right Triangle
sections.content: To use trigonometry, you must first label the three sides of a right triangle relative to a specific acute angle (often denoted as θ). The Hypotenuse is always the longest side, located directly across from the 90-degree angle. The Opposite side is the leg that does not touch the vertex of the angle θ. The Adjacent side is the leg that forms one side of the angle θ (along with the hypotenuse).

sections.title: The SOH CAH TOA Ratios
sections.content:
The three primary trigonometric ratios are defined as follows: Sine (sin) is the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the hypotenuse (sin θ = opp/hyp). Cosine (cos) is the ratio of the length of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse (cos θ = adj/hyp). Tangent (tan) is the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the adjacent side (tan θ = opp/adj).

![A flowchart showing the steps: Identify Angle, Label Sides (Opp, Adj, Hyp), Select Ratio (SOH CAH TOA), and Simplify Fraction.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/6703996a-8670-4144-8d1c-e1b6ef2bc117-1786505989006-307.webp)

sections.title: The Tangent Identity
sections.content: Beyond the side-ratio definition, tangent can also be expressed as the ratio of sine to cosine: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ. This is a useful check to ensure your individual sine and cosine calculations are consistent with your tangent calculation.

worked_examples.question: In right triangle XYZ, the right angle is at Y. Side XY = 7 and side YZ = 24. Find the value of cos(X).
worked_examples.solution: 1. Identify the sides relative to angle X. The side opposite X is YZ (24). The side adjacent to X is XY (7). 2. Calculate the hypotenuse (XZ) using the Pythagorean theorem: 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625. The square root of 625 is 25. 3. Apply the cosine ratio: cos(X) = adjacent / hypotenuse. 4. Substitute the values: cos(X) = 7 / 25.

worked_examples.question: Given a right triangle where sin(θ) = 3/5 and cos(θ) = 4/5, what is tan(θ)?
worked_examples.solution: 1. Use the identity tan(θ) = sin(θ) / cos(θ). 2. Substitute the known values: tan(θ) = (3/5) / (4/5). 3. Simplify the complex fraction by multiplying by the reciprocal: (3/5) * (5/4) = 3/4. Alternatively, recognize that if sin = 3/5 (opp/hyp) and cos = 4/5 (adj/hyp), then opp = 3 and adj = 4, so tan = 3/4.

common_mistakes: Confusing the opposite and adjacent sides by not looking at the triangle from the perspective of the specific angle requested.
Using the hypotenuse in the denominator for tangent (tan is opp/adj, not opp/hyp).
Forgetting to simplify the fraction to its lowest terms.
Swapping the numerator and denominator (e.g., calculating adj/opp for tangent).
exam_tips: Use the mnemonic SOH CAH TOA to remember the ratios: Sine-Opposite-Hypotenuse, Cosine-Adjacent-Hypotenuse, Tangent-Opposite-Adjacent.
Always identify the hypotenuse first; it is the only side that never changes regardless of which acute angle you are looking at.
If the ACT provides a ratio like sin(θ) = 0.6, convert it to a fraction (6/10 or 3/5) to easily identify side lengths.
content.recap: Trigonometric ratios describe the relationship between angles and side lengths in right triangles. Remember SOH CAH TOA: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, and tan = opp/adj. You can verify tangent by dividing sine by cosine.

knowledge_claims.content: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle and is always located opposite the 90-degree angle.
Relative to an acute angle θ, the opposite side is the leg that does not share a vertex with θ.
Relative to an acute angle θ, the adjacent side is the leg that forms one side of the angle θ.
The sine of an angle (sin θ) is calculated as the length of the opposite side divided by the length of the hypotenuse.
The cosine of an angle (cos θ) is calculated as the length of the adjacent side divided by the length of the hypotenuse.
The tangent of an angle (tan θ) is calculated as the length of the opposite side divided by the length of the adjacent side.
The tangent of an angle θ is equivalent to the ratio of sin θ divided by cos θ.
To find a missing side length needed for a trig ratio in a right triangle, apply the Pythagorean theorem (a² + b² = c²).
A common error is using the hypotenuse in the tangent ratio, which should only involve the two legs (opposite and adjacent).
In any right triangle, the sine and cosine values of an acute angle must always be less than 1 because the hypotenuse is the longest side.
The mnemonic SOH CAH TOA represents the three primary trigonometric ratios: Sine=Opp/Hyp, Cosine=Adj/Hyp, Tangent=Opp/Adj.
If the angle of interest changes from one acute angle to the other in the same triangle, the labels for 'opposite' and 'adjacent' swap.
